# Amonite

> Amonite is a GNU/Linux operating system engineered for what you do after install: desktop work, development, administration, and local AI. Its two public editions are Standard, the default complete desktop, and Lite, a minimal desktop assembled from independent components. Current releases: Lite (lite/v1.0.0-alpha) and Standard (v1.0.0-alpha.2).

Amonite is an independent distribution maintained by Manuel Gil. Every package ships because it delivers a meaningful capability, never because another package happened to recommend it. Standard provides an XFCE desktop; Lite provides a Labwc desktop with a Wayland session managed by UWSM. The official community is r/Amonite; official releases are published through GitHub Releases. The distribution source repository is github.com/ManuelGil/amonite, licensed GPL-3.0. There is no roadmap, newsletter, or support inbox on this site.

## Pages

- Official website: https://amonite.org/

- [Home](https://amonite.org/): What Amonite is and what becomes possible after install.
- [Philosophy](https://amonite.org/philosophy/): Why Amonite exists and the selection principle behind every included package.
- [Engineering](https://amonite.org/engineering/): How capabilities (desktop, development, administration, security, networking, local AI) are implemented, and what stays replaceable.
- [Gallery](https://amonite.org/gallery/): Unedited screenshots of the released system: first boot, terminal, welcome handbook, installer, and everyday tools.
- [Downloads](https://amonite.org/downloads/): ISO, SHA256 checksum, GPG signature, release notes, and installation guide for the current release.
- [Community](https://amonite.org/community/): r/Amonite for questions, feedback, bug reports, and discussion; GitHub Releases for official distribution.

## Facts

- Series: Nautilus (Version 1). Public editions: Lite, Standard. Current releases: Standard 1.0.0-alpha.2; Lite 1.0.0-alpha (lite/v1.0.0-alpha).
- Stage: Alpha. Both releases are intended for evaluation and testing, not production use.
- Release dates: Standard 1.0.0-alpha.2 published 2026-07-28; Lite 1.0.0-alpha published 2026-07-28; Standard 1.0.0-alpha published 2026-07-22.
- Architecture: amd64. Validated on 1 CPU core, 1 GiB RAM, 12 GiB storage, BIOS and UEFI, under QEMU/KVM. Installed size approximately 2.6 GiB.
- Base platform: Debian Stable. Standard desktop: XFCE. Lite desktop: Labwc with a Wayland session managed by UWSM. Default terminal: Kitty. Installer: Calamares.
- Capabilities: desktop computing, software development, system administration, local artificial intelligence (offline inference over GGUF models via llama.cpp with an OpenAI-compatible API), networking, security (AppArmor, optional encrypted installs), storage, documentation.
- ISO sizes: Standard 1.0.0-alpha.2 is 1,292,009,472 bytes; Lite 1.0.0-alpha is 1,283,014,656 bytes.
- Verification: every release publishes SHA256SUMS and detached GPG signatures (.asc) for the ISO, the checksum file, and a machine-readable release.json manifest.
- Maintainer: Manuel Gil (https://imgil.dev/).
- Source repository: https://github.com/ManuelGil/amonite (GPL-3.0)
- Releases: https://github.com/ManuelGil/amonite/releases
- Community: https://www.reddit.com/r/amonite/
